title: Exception-Aggregation Sink (Vague Try Blocks)
pattern: Aggregating highly distinct fallible operations (file system I/O, JSON parsing, business invariant verification) under a single, generic try-block or catch-all mapping that discards individual diagnostic contexts.
why_bad: Destroys diagnostic precision. If the operation fails, the caller cannot programmatically distinguish between a missing file, a corrupted JSON schema, or a business rule violation. This forces downstream error handlers to treat all failures identically or parse fragile error-string details.
detection: Look for functions where multiple different error-producing functions (returning different error types) are converted into a single vague error variant using a catch-all mapping (`map_err(|_| Error::Generic)` or `anyhow::Error` with no contextual enrichment).
counterexample: `Context-dependent`. Scripting or prototyping where speed is prioritized over diagnostic reliability, and where all errors are simply dumped to the console.
fix: Explicitly map and enrich each individual fallible step to its own distinct error variant, preserving the source error.
source: *John K. Ousterhout - A Philosophy of Software Design (2018)*, Chapter 10, "Define Errors Out of Existence" (Exception Aggregation); *Robert C. Martin - Clean Code (2008)*, Chapter 7, "Error Handling".
